A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the dust emission in the diffuse ISM is well characterized by a simple model, and that this model can be used to characterize the dust emission in other environments, for example the interstellar dust in the Galactic centre, or the dust in external galaxies.
we have shown that dust in the diffuse ISM is evolving, and that its SED flattens at millimetre frequencies.
we are able to measure the dust temperature, dust emissivity, dust opacity, dust spectral index, and dust spectral shape in the microwave range.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dust emissivity is a strong function of temperature.
there is a strong correlation between the dust and the HI emission.
the dust emission spectrum in the diffuse ISM is remarkably well described by a modified blackbody, with a temperature T and a dust emissivity index β.
